Notes on running Postgres upgrades

A major version upgrade with pg_upgrade in link mode takes minutes rather than hours, at the cost of having no way back other than a restore. Rehearse it against a copy of production before touching production.

The documentation on pg_upgrade lists the checks it runs up front, and running it with the check flag a week early surfaces the extension version mismatches that otherwise appear during the maintenance window.

Statistics do not survive the upgrade. Running ANALYZE afterwards is not optional, and skipping it produces a database that is up, responsive to a health check, and choosing terrible plans for every query that matters.

Keep the old cluster on disk until the new one has served a full business cycle. Disk is cheaper than the conversation about the backup that turned out to be untested.
